title.title: Positive bisectional curvature forces $\mathbb{C}^n$
title.subtitle: Claim: a complete noncompact Kähler manifold with positive bisectional curvature is biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^n$

plain: If an endless complex space curves positively in every complex direction, it is plain flat space in disguise

object.heading: Complete noncompact Kähler manifolds with bisectional curvature $> 0$

beats.text: Yau asked in 1982: is every such manifold just $\mathbb{C}^n$?
Every earlier proof needed maximal volume growth (Chau–Tam, Gang Liu, Lee–Tam)
The claim needs no curvature bound, no volume growth and no topology

steps: Run the Kähler–Ricci flow, which evens the curvature out
A new Harnack inequality keeps control, with no curvature bound
A 'volume clock' builds charts that glue into all of $\mathbb C^n$

achievement.label: Yau's uniformization conjecture (1982)
achievement.context: Before: every proof needed maximal volume growth (Chau–Tam, Gang Liu, Lee–Tam)
achievement.note: Earlier partial results also credit ChatGPT models, per the paper's footnote

voice.text: Positive curvature in every complex direction. Every earlier proof needed extra volume growth.
A flow and a volume clock build charts that glue into flat space.
Claimed: it is always complex Euclidean space.

sources.quote: Every earlier result needed maximal volume growth: Chau–Tam with bounded curvature, [Gang Liu](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.08958) and then Lee–Tam without it.
assumes only pointwise strict positivity: no curvature bound, no volume growth, no topology
